cues.en: I'm sure you are curious about the name of the title in this video.
cues.zh: 相信你對這支影片標題很好奇。

cues.en: Hella swag is an acronym and I will explain what it stands for towards the end of this video.
cues.zh: HellaSwag 是縮寫，影片後段會解釋全名。

cues.en: And before then, I will tell you about what it is and show a code demo of how to use it.
cues.zh: 在那之前，先介紹它是什麼，再示範如何使用。

cues.en: Hella swag is a benchmark evaluation test that people use for LL.
cues.zh: HellaSwag 是用來評估 LLM 的基準測驗。

cues.en: It is different from token based evals like perplexity.
cues.zh: 不同於困惑度等詞元層級評估，

cues.en: Instead, it's kind of like giving an LLM a multiple choice exam, where the correct answer depends
cues.zh: 它比較像讓 LLM 考選擇題，正確答案取決於

cues.en: on understanding proper syntax and grammar, and also on having world knowledge in a broad range of topics.
cues.zh: 是否理解句法、文法，以及廣泛領域的世界知識。

cues.en: I will show you how it's implemented in the Python demo, and here you can see an example of two test questions.
cues.zh: Python 會示範實作，這裡先看兩題例子。

cues.en: So the idea is that we present the model with the first part of a text, which is called the context.
cues.zh: 先給模型一段文字的開頭，稱為 context，語境。

cues.en: So here the context is a bearded man is seen speaking into the camera and making several faces.
cues.zh: 這裡是：「一名留鬍子的男子對著鏡頭說話，做出各種表情。」

cues.en: The man okay, that is the context.
cues.zh: 「這名男子……」，這就是語境。

cues.en: Then there are four candidate endings, one of which is correct.
cues.zh: 接著有四個候選結尾，其中一個正確。

cues.en: In this example it's option D which is bolded.
cues.zh: 這題是粗體的 D。

cues.en: So the model is given the context and then all of the endings.
cues.zh: 模型取得語境與全部結尾。

cues.en: And then you calculate the model's probabilities associated with each ending.
cues.zh: 再計算每個結尾的相關機率。

cues.en: If the model has the highest probabilities for the correct ending, then we consider the model to have gotten that question correct.
cues.zh: 若正確結尾的機率最高，就認為答對。

cues.en: And that's what this blue highlight indicates here.
cues.zh: 藍色標示的就是這點。

cues.en: And now in this example the correct response was again D.
cues.zh: 另一題正確答案同樣是 D，

cues.en: But the model guessed option A.
cues.zh: 但模型猜 A，

cues.en: So it was technically wrong here.
cues.zh: 所以技術上答錯。

cues.en: So that's the general idea.
cues.zh: 概念就是這樣。

cues.en: Now, how exactly do we quantify the model's choice for each of these four options?
cues.zh: 那如何量化模型對四個選項的選擇？

cues.en: That's what you will see in the Python demo.
cues.zh: Python 示範會看到。

cues.en: So which one of these four options is really supposed to follow this context over here?
cues.zh: 也就是哪個選項，真正應該接在這段語境後面？

cues.en: Here is a plot that illustrates how the quantification works.
cues.zh: 這張圖說明量化方式。

cues.en: So for this particular example there were 21 tokens in the context.
cues.zh: 這個例子的語境有 21 個詞元。

cues.en: And then the blue and the red lines here correspond to the model's final output logits for the upcoming token.
cues.zh: 藍線與紅線，對應模型對接下來詞元的最終輸出 logits。

cues.en: Now there are four endings in each sample, but I'm only showing here just the correct one in blue and one of the incorrect endings in red.
cues.zh: 每筆有四個結尾，這裡只畫正確的藍線，以及其中一個錯誤的紅線。

cues.en: You can see that the token probabilities for the correct endings are across all of these tokens, higher
cues.zh: 可以看到，正確結尾各詞元的機率，整體

cues.en: than the probabilities for the incorrect endings.
cues.zh: 高於錯誤結尾。

cues.en: Now these are the softmax probabilities for each individual token.
cues.zh: 這些是每個詞元各自的 softmax 機率。

cues.en: So their sum is actually going to be greater than one.
cues.zh: 所以加起來，其實會大於 1。

cues.en: And actually in the real quantification the log probability is used, not the actual probability values.
cues.zh: 真正量化時，用對數機率，不是直接用機率值。

cues.en: I will get into that in more detail when I switch to code.
cues.zh: 切到程式會再說明。

cues.en: But basically that's just to reduce the risk of numerical issues.
cues.zh: 基本上，是為了降低數值問題風險。

cues.en: And here I'm showing the sum.
cues.zh: 這裡顯示總和。

cues.en: But you actually need to multiply multiply probabilities.
cues.zh: 但其實應該把機率相乘。

cues.en: And because these probabilities are really tiny, their products are even tinier.
cues.zh: 因為機率很小，相乘後更小，

cues.en: So therefore we sum the logs instead of multiplying the probabilities.
cues.zh: 所以改成加總對數，而不是乘機率。

cues.en: And then I'm looping through and getting the logit for each upcoming token.
cues.zh: 接著逐一取得每個接下來詞元的 logit。

cues.en: So this is always a little bit tricky when you're working with a GPT architecture where you're trying to predict the next token in a sequence.
cues.zh: GPT 架構預測下一詞元時，這點總有些棘手。

cues.en: What you actually want is the logits preceding the token in the token sequence.
cues.zh: 真正要的，是序列裡該詞元前一個位置的 logits。

cues.en: Because the idea is that as the model is processing each token, it's transforming that token into a prediction for the next token.
cues.zh: 因為處理目前詞元時，模型會把它轉成下一詞元的預測。

cues.en: So you don't want the processing of the next token.
cues.zh: 不是要處理下一個詞元後的結果，

cues.en: You want the end result of processing the current token.
cues.zh: 而是處理目前詞元的最終結果，

cues.en: And that is going to predict the next token.
cues.zh: 用來預測下一個。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So this is for the entire sequence of the correct prompt and the entire sequence for the incorrect prompt.
cues.zh: 這是正確提示與錯誤提示的完整序列。

cues.zh: 兩個提示開頭相同，

cues.en: The context is exactly the same in the beginning for these two options, and they differ only by this ending.

cues.zh: 所以不需要，

cues.en: We don't need to calculate any of the logits for the context because those will be exactly the same.
cues.zh: 不必計算語境的 logits，因為完全相同。

cues.zh: 只處理、加總兩個結尾所有詞元的 logits。

cues.zh: 但看完整結尾的所有詞元，

cues.en: the logits is higher for the correct ending, and it's lower for the incorrect ending.
cues.zh: 正確結尾的 logits 總和較高，錯誤的較低。

cues.en: On a whole, when we look at all of the tokens together.
cues.zh: 也就是整體看全部詞元。

cues.en: Now why am I summing the log softmax and not just the regular softmax probabilities?
cues.zh: 那為什麼加總 log_softmax，而不是一般 softmax 機率？

cues.en: If we want to get the probability of the entire ending so we can visualize that, I actually prefer that visualization.

cues.en: So if I just get rid of that log here and I just have softmax, we see it's exactly the same sentence.

cues.en: Everything is the same.

cues.en: It's just that these are now the probabilities instead of the log softmax probabilities.
cues.zh: 只是現在是機率，而非對數機率。

cues.en: As I mentioned in the slides, these numbers do not sum to one.
cues.zh: 如投影片所說，這些數字加起來不是 1。

cues.en: They sum to some number that's over one.
cues.zh: 總和大於 1。

cues.en: And that's because each one of these individual tokens is coming from a probability distribution over all 50,000 tokens.
cues.zh: 因為每個個別詞元的機率，來自對全部五萬詞元的機率分布，

cues.en: For this one token index.
cues.zh: 針對這一個序列位置。

cues.en: So the softmax probability is not over this token position.
cues.zh: softmax 的機率不是對這些序列位置計算，

cues.en: It's over all of the 50,000 tokens in the vocab separately calculated for each individual token.
cues.zh: 而是對詞彙表五萬個詞元，在每個位置各自計算。

cues.en: And that is why these numbers do not sum to one.
cues.zh: 所以這些數字加起來，不會是 1。

cues.en: However, when we are looking for the joint probability of this entire sentence, that's the probability of each of these tokens being selected.
cues.zh: 但要找整句的聯合機率，也就是各詞元被選到的機率，

cues.en: You do not sum the probabilities.
cues.zh: 不能把機率相加，

cues.en: You have to multiply the probabilities.
cues.zh: 必須相乘。

cues.en: And these probabilities can get very small.
cues.zh: 這些機率可能很小，

cues.en: They can be really really close to zero.
cues.zh: 非常接近零。

cues.en: And so the more tiny tiny numbers you multiply that are really close to zero.
cues.zh: 越多極小、接近零的數相乘，

cues.en: The product is going to be so absolutely tiny that you're basically working at, or possibly even below the precision of your computers.
cues.zh: 乘積就小到逼近，甚至低於電腦精度。

cues.en: So therefore, multiplying very tiny probabilities becomes very numerically unstable.
cues.zh: 因此，直接相乘很小的機率，數值非常不穩定。

cues.en: And that's why summing the logs is much more numerically stable.
cues.zh: 加總對數就穩定得多。

cues.en: A better thing to do is to sum the logs instead of multiplying the probabilities.
cues.zh: 比較好的方式，是加總對數，而非相乘機率。

cues.en: You need to know how that game works.
cues.zh: 知道遊戲怎麼玩。

cues.en: Otherwise, it's not really clear which one of these endings is going to be correct.
cues.zh: 否則，哪個結尾正確並不清楚。

cues.en: So that is why this is an interesting evaluation method, because it tells us not only about the model's
cues.zh: 所以，這種評估很有趣，不只反映模型

cues.en: ability to process individual tokens and sequences of tokens, but also about the model's world knowledge, the model's understanding of lots of different topics about the world.
cues.zh: 處理個別詞元與序列的能力，也反映世界知識、對各種主題的理解。

cues.en: In this slide, I will discuss a few limitations of hella swag.
cues.zh: 這張談 HellaSwag 的一些限制。

cues.en: For one thing, it requires domain specific performance in the test.
cues.zh: 第一，需要特定領域知識來作答。

cues.en: So let's say you have a model fine tuned for helping you write LinkedIn posts.
cues.zh: 假設模型微調成幫你寫 LinkedIn 貼文。

cues.en: And maybe it's a fantastic model and it's even better than the latest ChatGPT.
cues.zh: 也許很出色，甚至勝過最新 ChatGPT。

cues.en: But it does poorly on hella swag because you haven't trained your model to know about men's shaving
cues.zh: 但 HellaSwag 很差，因為沒訓練它理解男性刮鬍

cues.en: commercials and beer pong and other like esoteric topics that the Hella Swag dataset includes.
cues.zh: 廣告、啤酒乒乓球，以及資料集裡其他冷門主題。

cues.en: And a general issue with eval methods is that once a training set is published and a description of
cues.zh: 一般評估也有問題：訓練集與方法

cues.en: the assessment is public knowledge, LLM development companies can start to fine tune their models on
cues.zh: 一旦公開，LLM 公司就能開始用

cues.en: the training and the dev sets, and on other texts that are going to be similar to the test set.
cues.zh: train、dev，以及類似 test 的其他文本微調。

cues.en: So even if the Hella Swag team keeps their test set at hidden.
cues.zh: 即使 HellaSwag 團隊把 test 藏起來，

cues.en: The LMS can still be well prepared for it.
cues.zh: LLM 仍能準備充分。

cues.en: It's the same thing as when you study for an exam by going through previous exams in the same topic.
cues.zh: 就像你用同主題歷屆試題準備考試。

cues.en: Now, you might not know the exact exam questions that you will get, but if you study a lot of similar exams, you're likely to do better.
cues.zh: 不知道會考哪題，但多做類似考題，通常考得更好。

cues.en: So that means that these eval methods are often less indicative of real model capabilities after a few years.
cues.zh: 所以，過幾年後，評估方法常常就不太能代表模型真實能力。

cues.en: And yeah, as you saw, if you look through this data set, you will find some typos, some grammatical errors, and some sentences that just don't seem to make a whole lot of sense.
cues.zh: 如剛才看到，資料集有拼字、文法錯誤，也有不太通的句子。

cues.en: So it's not a super clean data set.
cues.zh: 所以，不算非常乾淨。

cues.en: Now, there are other groups that have tried to improve upon the evaluation, and every year there are
cues.zh: 其他團隊也嘗試改善評估，每年都有

cues.en: new assessments that are related to the idea of hella swag that are released, but still, Hella Swag is a pretty standard benchmark test.
cues.zh: 與 HellaSwag 概念相關的新測驗，但它仍是相當標準的基準。

cues.en: Okay, here we go.
cues.zh: 好，現在揭曉。

cues.en: Harder endings, longer contexts, and low shot activities for situations with adversarial generations.
cues.zh: 「更難的結尾、更長的語境，以及採對抗生成之情境的少樣本活動。」

cues.en: I'm like 99.999% sure that the authors first decided that they wanted to call it hella swag, and then
cues.zh: 我有 99.999% 把握，作者是先決定叫 HellaSwag，

cues.en: they had to come up with some fancy sounding words that matched those letters.
cues.zh: 再湊一些聽起來厲害、符合字母的詞。

cues.en: Okay, you are now familiar with two families of quantitative evaluations, those based on processing
cues.zh: 好，你現在認識兩類量化評估：

cues.en: individual tokens and those based on processing sequences of tokens.
cues.zh: 處理個別詞元，以及處理詞元序列。

cues.en: No method is perfect because language is complex and sloppy, and because llms are being developed much faster than the evaluations of those llms.
cues.zh: 沒有完美方法，因為語言複雜、雜亂，而 LLM 的開發又比評估進步得快。
